what: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
text: Modification rgl::axis3d() adds two extra parameters, ticksize labeldist, independently control length axis tick marks distance tick marks labels. Based solution proposed Stack Overflow (see References).

title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
code: axis3(   edge,   at = NULL,   labels = TRUE,   tick = TRUE,   line = TRUE,   pos = NULL,   nticks = 5,   ticksize = 0.05,   labeldist = 3,   ... )

title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
text: edge character string indicating edge bounding box axis drawn (format rgl::axis3d(), e.g. "z+-"). positions tick marks drawn; NULL computed automatically pretty(). labels tick labels: logical, indicating whether automatically label axes omitted, vector labels. tick logical; TRUE axis tick marks drawn. line logical; TRUE axis line drawn. pos optional position axis (see rgl::axis3d()). nticks approximate number tick marks = NULL. ticksize length tick marks, fraction distance center scene's range. labeldist distance tick marks labels, multiple ticksize. ... additional arguments passed rgl::segments3d() rgl::text3d().

title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
text: rglId object (see rgl::lowlevel()) identifiers rgl elements added (line, tick marks labels).

title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3
text: Dominic Woolf (2013, Mar 23). R rgl distance axis ticks tick labels, Stack Overflow, https://stackoverflow.com//39299740/4303451.

title: 3D axis with control over tick length and label position — axis3

what: Utilities for plotting with a categorical legend — categorical-color
title: Utilities for plotting with a categorical legend — categorical-color
text: hcld.colors() hot.colors() create color table useful coding qualitative information fcolor() assigns colors categorical (factor) values.

title: Utilities for plotting with a categorical legend — categorical-color
code: fcolor(f, col = hcld.colors(length(labels)), labels = levels(as.factor(f)))  hcld.colors(n, palette = "Dark 3", ...)  cat.colors(n)

title: Utilities for plotting with a categorical legend — categorical-color
text: f (factor, vector coercible factor) values converted colors. col colors level. Defaults hcld.colors(). labels levels use. Defaults levels(.factor(f)). n number colors (>= 1) palette. palette valid palette name hcl.colors() (one hcl.pals()). ... additional arguments passed legend().

title: Utilities for plotting with a categorical legend — categorical-color
text: fcolor() returns vector colors, one per element f. hcld.colors() cat.colors() return character vector colors (similar hcl.colors() rainbow(); see rgb()).

what: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
title: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
text: jet.colors hot.colors create color table useful contiguous color scales scolor assigns colors numerical vector.

title: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
code: scolor(s, col = jet.colors(128), slim = range(s, finite = TRUE))  jet.colors(n)  hot.colors(n, rev = TRUE)

title: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
text: s values converted color scale. col color table used set color scale (see image details). slim limits used set color scale. n number colors (>= 1) palette. rev logical; TRUE, palette reversed (decreasing overall luminosity).

title: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
text: scolor, jet.colors hot.colors return character vector colors.

title: Utilities for plotting with a continuous color scale — continuous-color
text: scolor converts real valued vector color scale. range slim divided length(col) + 1 pieces equal length. Values fall outside range scale coded NA. jet.colors generates rainbow style color table similar MATLAB (TM) jet color scheme. may appropriate distinguish values central value (e.g. positive negative values). hot.colors generates color table similar MATLAB (TM) hot color scheme (reversed default). may appropriate represent values ranging 0 maximum level (e.g. density estimation). default value rev = TRUE may adequate grayscale conversion.

what: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
title: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
text: fplot() designed combine standard R plot categorical (factor) legend. Analogous splot(), splits plotting region main panel legend panel, uses legend() draw labels colors symbols.

title: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
code: fplot(   labels,   col = hcld.colors(length(labels)),   type = c("box", "point", "line"),   pch = 16,   lty = 1,   lwd = 2,   cex = 1,   border = col,   pt.cex = cex * 1.5,   seg.len = 1.5,   horizontal = FALSE,   legend.shrink = 1,   legend.width = NULL,   legend.mar = NULL,   legend.lab = NULL,   legend.x = "center",   bigplot = NULL,   smallplot = NULL,   add = FALSE,   ... )

title: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
text: labels vector category labels. col colors associated level (order labels). Defaults hcld3.colors(). type type symbols shown legend: "box" filled color boxes (classic factor-level legend), "point" points, "line" line segments. pch plotting ‘character’ (symbol) used type = "point". lty, lwd line types widths lines appearing legend, type = "line". cex text/symbol size legend. border, pt.cex, seg.len additional legend() parameters, also used estimate required legend width/height. default values : border = col, pt.cex = cex * 1.5 seg.len = 1.5. horizontal logical; FALSE (default) legend appear right side. TRUE legend along bottom. legend.shrink amount shrink size legend relative full height width plot. legend.width, legend.mar control size margin legend panel, splot(). left NULL (default), computed automatically following character-size logic legend() uses internally. legend.lab legend title. legend.x legend location relative legend panel (argument x legend()). Possible values : "center" (default), "bottomright", "bottom", "bottomleft", "left", "topleft", "top", "topright" "right". bigplot, smallplot plot coordinates main legend panels. passed determined within function. add logical; TRUE legend just added existing plot (graphical parameters changed). ... additional arguments passed legend().

title: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
text: fplot() invisibly returns list components: bigplot, smallplot, old.par, col labels (par(old.par) reset plot parameters values entering function).

title: Add a categorical legend to an standard R plot — fplot
code: # Plot equivalent to fpoints(): f <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl) res <- fplot(levels(f), col = cat.colors(nlevels(f)), type = "point",              legend.lab = "cyl") with( mtcars, plot(hp, qsec, col = fcolor(f, col = res$col),                    pch = 16, cex = 1.5, main = "Motor Trend Car Road Tests"))  par(res$old.par) # restore graphical parameters

what: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
title: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
text: Splits active rgl device two subscenes (main plot legend) draws, legend subscene, legend subscene, colored categorical legend together corresponding labels.

title: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
code: fplot3d(   labels,   col = hcld.colors(length(labels)),   legend.zoom = 0.6,   legend.width = 0.1,   legend.mar = 0.2,   legend.lab = NULL,   lab.dist = 2.5,   lab.rev = FALSE,   ... )

title: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
text: labels vector legend labels (one level per category). Defaults seq_along(col). col vector colors associated label (defaults hcld.colors(length(labels))). legend.zoom zoom factor applied legend subscene/panel legend.width relative size legend spheres, fraction corresponding dimension legend subscene. legend.mar relative width legend panel, fraction total device width. legend.lab legend title. lab.dist distance spheres text labels. lab.rev logical; TRUE order levels legend reversed (default shown top bottom). ... additional arguments passed axis3().

title: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
text: Invisibly returns identifiers created subscenes (see rgl::layout3d()).

title: Add a categorical legend to an 'rgl' plot — fplot3d
text: 3D plot

what: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
title: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
text: Draws triangular mesh (mesh3d) colored according levels factor f, automatically adding categorical legend (via fplot3d()).

title: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
code: fshade3d(   x,   f,   meshColor = c("faces", "vertices"),   labels = levels(f),   col = hcld.colors(length(labels)),   legend.zoom = 1,   legend.width = 0.1,   legend.mar = 0.15,   legend.lab = NULL,   lab.dist = 3,   lab.rev = FALSE,   add = FALSE,   ... )

title: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
text: x triangular mesh (mesh3d object, see rgl::mesh3d()). f factor used color mesh. values interpreted depends meshColor. meshColor determines color applied mesh: "faces" "vertices" (see rgl::shade3d()). labels legend labels (defaults levels(f)). col vector colors associated level f (default generated col.pal). legend.zoom zoom factor applied legend subscene/panel legend.width relative size legend spheres, fraction corresponding dimension legend subscene. legend.mar relative width legend panel, fraction total device width. legend.lab legend title. lab.dist distance spheres text labels. lab.rev logical; TRUE order levels legend reversed (default shown top bottom). add logical; TRUE legend redrawn (useful adding several meshes already existing legend). ... additional arguments passed rgl::shade3d().

title: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
text: Called side effect (draws mesh , unless add = TRUE, legend active rgl device); invisibly returns object identifiers.

title: Draw 3D mesh objects adding a categorical legend — fshade3d
text: 3D plot
code:

#ifdef GL_FRAGMENT_PRECISION_HIGH

#else

#endif
#endif
varying vec4 vCol; // carries alpha
varying vec4 vPosition;
#if defined(HAS_TEXTURE) || defined (IS_TEXT)
varying vec2 vTexcoord;
uniform sampler2D uSampler;
#endif

#ifdef HAS_FOG
uniform int uFogMode;
uniform vec3 uFogColor;
uniform vec4 uFogParms;
#endif

varying vec4 vNormal;
#endif

uniform vec4 vClipplane[NCLIPPLANES];
#endif

uniform mat4 mvMatrix;
#endif

uniform vec3 emission;
uniform float shininess;
#if NLIGHTS > 0
uniform vec3 ambient[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 specular[NLIGHTS]; // light*material
uniform vec3 diffuse[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 lightDir[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool viewpoint[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool finite[NLIGHTS];
#endif
#endif // IS_LIT

#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
uniform bool front;
varying float normz;
#endif

#ifdef FAT_LINES
varying vec2 vPoint;
varying float vLength;
#endif

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
varying vec3 vReflection;
#endif

void main(void) {
  vec4 fragColor;
#ifdef FAT_LINES
  vec2 point = vPoint;
  bool neg = point.y < 0.0;
  point.y = neg ? (point.y + vLength)/(1.0 - vLength) :
                 -(point.y - vLength)/(1.0 - vLength);
#if defined(IS_TRANSPARENT) && defined(IS_LINESTRIP)
  if (neg && length(point) <= 1.0) discard;
#endif
  point.y = min(point.y, 0.0);
  if (length(point) > 1.0) discard;
#endif // FAT_LINES
  
#ifdef ROUND_POINTS
  vec2 coord = gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5);
  if (length(coord) > 0.5) discard;
#endif
  
#if NCLIPPLANES > 0
  for (int i = 0; i < NCLIPPLANES; i++)
    if (dot(vPosition, vClipplane[i]) < 0.0) discard;
#endif
    
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    vec3 n = vec3(0., 0., 1.);
#elif defined(IS_LIT)
    vec3 n = normalize(vNormal.xyz);
#endif
    
#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
    if ((normz <= 0.) != front) discard;
#endif

#ifdef IS_LIT
    vec3 eye = normalize(-vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
    vec3 lightdir;
    vec4 colDiff;
    vec3 halfVec;
    vec4 lighteffect = vec4(emission, 0.);
    vec3 col;
    float nDotL;
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    n = -faceforward(n, n, eye);
#endif

    // Simulate two-sided lighting
    if (n.z < 0.0)

      lightdir = lightDir[i];

#endif

    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance
 
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)

#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb,

#if defined(IS_LIT) && !defined(FIXED_QUADS)
varying vec4 vNormal;
#endif

#if NCLIPPLANES > 0
uniform vec4 vClipplane[NCLIPPLANES];
#endif

#if NLIGHTS > 0
uniform mat4 mvMatrix;
#endif

#ifdef IS_LIT
uniform vec3 emission;
uniform float shininess;
#if NLIGHTS > 0
uniform vec3 ambient[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 specular[NLIGHTS]; // light*material
uniform vec3 diffuse[NLIGHTS];
uniform vec3 lightDir[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool viewpoint[NLIGHTS];
uniform bool finite[NLIGHTS];
#endif
#endif // IS_LIT

#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
uniform bool front;
varying float normz;
#endif

#ifdef FAT_LINES
varying vec2 vPoint;
varying float vLength;
#endif

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
varying vec3 vReflection;
#endif

void main(void) {
  vec4 fragColor;
#ifdef FAT_LINES
  vec2 point = vPoint;
  bool neg = point.y < 0.0;
  point.y = neg ? (point.y + vLength)/(1.0 - vLength) :
                 -(point.y - vLength)/(1.0 - vLength);
#if defined(IS_TRANSPARENT) && defined(IS_LINESTRIP)
  if (neg && length(point) <= 1.0) discard;
#endif
  point.y = min(point.y, 0.0);
  if (length(point) > 1.0) discard;
#endif // FAT_LINES
  
#ifdef ROUND_POINTS
  vec2 coord = gl_PointCoord - vec2(0.5);
  if (length(coord) > 0.5) discard;
#endif
  
#if NCLIPPLANES > 0
  for (int i = 0; i < NCLIPPLANES; i++)
    if (dot(vPosition, vClipplane[i]) < 0.0) discard;
#endif
    
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    vec3 n = vec3(0., 0., 1.);
#elif defined(IS_LIT)
    vec3 n = normalize(vNormal.xyz);
#endif
    
#ifdef IS_TWOSIDED
    if ((normz <= 0.) != front) discard;
#endif

#ifdef IS_LIT
    vec3 eye = normalize(-vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
    vec3 lightdir;
    vec4 colDiff;
    vec3 halfVec;
    vec4 lighteffect = vec4(emission, 0.);
    vec3 col;
    float nDotL;
#ifdef FIXED_QUADS
    n = -faceforward(n, n, eye);
#endif
    
#if NLIGHTS > 0
    // Simulate two-sided lighting
    if (n.z < 0.0)
      n = -n;
    for (int i=0;i<NLIGHTS;i++) {
      colDiff = vec4(vCol.rgb * diffuse[i], vCol.a);
      lightdir = lightDir[i];
      if (!viewpoint[i]) {
        if (finite[i]) {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 1.)).xyz;
        } else {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 0.)).xyz;
        }
      }
      if (!finite[i]) {
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      } else {
        lightdir = normalize(lightdir - vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      }
      col = ambient[i];
      nDotL = dot(n, lightdir);
      col = col + max(nDotL, 0.) * colDiff.rgb;
      col = col + pow(max(dot(halfVec, n), 0.), shininess) * specular[i];
      lighteffect = lighteffect + vec4(col, colDiff.a);
    }
#endif
    
#else // not IS_LIT
    vec4 colDiff = vCol;
    vec4 lighteffect = colDiff;
#endif
    
#ifdef IS_TEXT
    vec4 textureColor = lighteffect*texture2D(uSampler, vTexcoord);
#endif
    
#ifdef HAS_TEXTURE

// These calculations use the definitions from 
// https://docs.gl/gl3/glTexEnv

#ifdef USE_ENVMAP
    float m = 2.0 * sqrt(dot(vReflection, vReflection) + 2.0*vReflection.z + 1.0);
    vec4 textureColor = texture2D(uSampler, vReflection.xy / m + vec2(0.5, 0.5));
#else
    vec4 textureColor = texture2D(uSampler, vTexcoord);
#endif

#ifdef TEXTURE_rgb

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(textureColor.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = lighteffect*vec4(textureColor.rgb, 1.);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.rgb) * lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb + textureColor.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif //TEXTURE_rgb
        
#ifdef TEXTURE_rgba

#ifdef TEXMODE_replace
// already done
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = lighteffect*textureColor;
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_decal
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.a)*lighteffect.rgb) +
                     textureColor.a*textureColor.rgb, 
                     lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - textureColor.rgb) * lighteffect.rgb,
                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb + textureColor.rgb,
                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif
    
#endif //TEXTURE_rgba
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb, luminance);
#endif 

#if defined(TEXMODE_modulate) || defined(TEXMODE_blend) || defined(TEXMODE_add)
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a*luminance);
#endif
 
#endif // TEXTURE_alpha
    
// The TEXTURE_luminance values are not from that reference    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(luminance, luminance, luminance, lighteffect.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance
 
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(luminance, luminance, luminance, textureColor.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);

#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    
    fragColor = textureColor;

#elif defined(IS_TEXT)
    if (textureColor.a < 0.1)
      discard;
    else
      fragColor = textureColor;
#else
    fragColor = lighteffect;
#endif // HAS_TEXTURE
    
#ifdef HAS_FOG
    // uFogParms elements: x = near, y = far, z = fogscale, w = (1-sin(FOV/2))/(1+sin(FOV/2))
    // In Exp and Exp2: use density = density/far
    // fogF will be the proportion of fog
    // Initialize it to the linear value
    float fogF;
    if (uFogMode > 0) {
      fogF = (uFogParms.y - vPosition.z/vPosition.w)/(uFogParms.y - uFogParms.x);
      if (uFogMode > 1)
        fogF = mix(uFogParms.w, 1.0, fogF);
      fogF = fogF*uFogParms.z;
      if (uFogMode == 2)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF);
      // Docs are wrong: use (density*c)^2, not density*c^2
      // https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/master/src/mesa/swrast/s_fog.c#L58
      else if (uFogMode == 3)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF*fogF);
      fogF = clamp(fogF, 0.0, 1.0);
      gl_FragColor = vec4(mix(fragColor.rgb, uFogColor, fogF), fragColor.a);
    } else gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#else
    gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#endif // HAS_FOG

title: Utilities for setting the 'rgl' mouse actions — mouse-actions
text: none, left, right, middle, wheel actions corresponding mouse button; see parameter mouseMode rgl::par3d(). button mouse button panning configured. Use 1 left, 2 right, 3 middle, 4 wheel, 0 set action button pressed. dev rgl device callback configured. Defaults active device (see rgl::cur3d()). subscene subscene callback configured. Defaults device's active subscene. message whether print message confirming configured button, device subscene.

title: Utilities for setting the 'rgl' mouse actions — mouse-actions
text: setmousemode() invisibly returns resulting mouseMode vector. pan3d() called side effect (registers mouse callbacks); optionally prints message confirming configured button, device subscene.

title: Utilities for setting the 'rgl' mouse actions — mouse-actions
text: setmousemode() sets mouse button mode current new rgl devices (via rgl::par3d()). pan3d() configures callback functions mouse button dragging pans active subscene (opened) rgl device.

      lightdir = lightDir[i];

        if (finite[i]) {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 1.)).xyz;
        } else {
          lightdir = (mvMatrix * vec4(lightdir, 0.)).xyz;
        }
      }
      if (!finite[i]) {
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      } else {
        lightdir = normalize(lightdir - vPosition.xyz/vPosition.w);
        halfVec = normalize(lightdir + eye);
      }
      col = ambient[i];
      nDotL = dot(n, lightdir);
      col = col + max(nDotL, 0.) * colDiff.rgb;
      col = col + pow(max(dot(halfVec, n), 0.), shininess) * specular[i];

#endif

    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb + textureColor.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif //TEXTURE_rgb

#endif

#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_decal

#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend

                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add

                    lighteffect.a*textureColor.a);
#endif
    
#endif //TEXTURE_rgba
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_alpha

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(lighteffect.rgb, luminance);
#endif

#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, lighteffect.a);
#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance
 
    
#ifdef TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    float luminance = dot(vec3(1.,1.,1.),textureColor.rgb)/3.;

#if defined(TEXMODE_replace) || defined(TEXMODE_decal)
    textureColor = vec4(luminance, luminance, luminance, textureColor.a);
#endif 

#ifdef TEXMODE_modulate
    textureColor = vec4(luminance*lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_blend
    textureColor = vec4((1. - luminance)*lighteffect.rgb,
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);
#endif

#ifdef TEXMODE_add
    textureColor = vec4(luminance + lighteffect.rgb, 
                        textureColor.a*lighteffect.a);

#endif

#endif // TEXTURE_luminance_alpha
    
    fragColor = textureColor;

    if (textureColor.a < 0.1)
      discard;
    else
      fragColor = textureColor;
#else
    fragColor = lighteffect;
#endif // HAS_TEXTURE

    // In Exp and Exp2: use density = density/far
    // fogF will be the proportion of fog
    // Initialize it to the linear value
    float fogF;
    if (uFogMode > 0) {
      fogF = (uFogParms.y - vPosition.z/vPosition.w)/(uFogParms.y - uFogParms.x);
      if (uFogMode > 1)
        fogF = mix(uFogParms.w, 1.0, fogF);
      fogF = fogF*uFogParms.z;
      if (uFogMode == 2)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF);
      // Docs are wrong: use (density*c)^2, not density*c^2
      // https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/master/src/mesa/swrast/s_fog.c#L58
      else if (uFogMode == 3)
        fogF = 1.0 - exp(-fogF*fogF);
      fogF = clamp(fogF, 0.0, 1.0);
      gl_FragColor = vec4(mix(fragColor.rgb, uFogColor, fogF), fragColor.a);
    } else gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#else
    gl_FragColor = fragColor;
#endif // HAS_FOG

code: # Plot equivalent to spoints(): scale.range <- range(mtcars$mpg) res <- splot(slim = scale.range, legend.lab = "mpg") with( mtcars, plot(hp, qsec, col = scolor(mpg, slim = scale.range),       pch = 16, cex = 1.5, main = "Motor Trend Car Road Tests"))  par(res$old.par) # restore graphical parameters # Multiple plots with a common legend: # regularly spaced 2D data... set.seed(1) nx <- c(40, 40) # ndata =  prod(nx) x1 <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = nx[1]) x2 <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = nx[2]) trend <- outer(x1, x2, function(x,y) x^2 - y^2) y <- trend + rnorm(prod(nx), 0, 0.1) scale.range <- c(-1.2, 1.2) scale.color <- jet.colors(256) # 1x2 plot with some room for the legend... old.par <- par(mfrow = c(1,2), omd = c(0.05, 0.85, 0.05, 0.95)) image( x1, x2, trend, zlim = scale.range, main = 'Trend', col = scale.color) image( x1, x2, y, zlim = scale.range, main = 'Data', col = scale.color) par(old.par) # the legend can be added to any plot... splot(slim = scale.range, col = scale.color, legend.shrink = 0.7, add = TRUE)  ## note that argument 'zlim' in 'image' corresponds with 'slim' in 'sxxxx' functions.
